as_told.title: Woman's death witnessed at LAX, time slows and sound returns

plain: At Los Angeles International Airport in the 1980s, Brent Friedman says he was beside a woman who had been struck and was dying, and although the airport "is a very noisy place," he "heard nothing except her breathing," time seemed to slow, and the moment she died "all of the noise came back." Friedman, a guest on an episode about Hollywood and the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, tells it as something he lived through himself, a moment where ordinary reality seemed to pause around a death.
